title: Release Symphony: Steward Cheatpad (WIP)
content:
Purpose / pitch:
This is a compact, practical cheatpad for the person running a progressive release (the Steward). It frames the canary/A-B runway as a "Release Symphony" — where the steward conducts visibility, cadence, and fallbacks rather than micromanaging every instrument.

Intended audience:
- Release Steward (primary)
- Product owners & PMs
- SRE/oncall recipient
- Observability + Data engineer support
- Solutions/SE on call for customer-facing cohorts

Why a small cheatpad?
- Most rollouts fail at coordination and signal translation, not technical correctness.
- The Steward needs a single page of actions, a short script for comms, and a checklist for common failure modes.

Quick run sequence (5–40 minutes depending on stage):
1) Preflight (5–10m) — confirm readiness
   - Canary config live and matches plan (model/version/route). Ticket ENG-7843 
   - Traffic slice created and tagged in routing config (slice-id = rs-yyyymmdd-01)
   - Observability dashboards up: latency, p50/p95/p99, error rate, token cost, model divergence (BLEU/ROUGE-ish for regen), human-flag rate.
   - Synthetic probe run: 50 synthetic requests through canary path; validate no 5xx, latency within SLO.

2) Activation (1–5m) — flip and announce
   - Activate slice to 0.5% (or configured) and post to #rollouts and email watchers.
   - Set a 30m timer: early-watch window.

3) Early watch (30–60m) — human eyes + auto rules
   - Look at human-flag and error spikes first. If any above threshold escalate (see thresholds below).
   - Check distribution: are errors concentrated in a cohort, route, or user agent?

4) Ramp plan (hours–days)
   - Minute-by-minute automation for first 2% (watch & hold rules), then step increases at pre-agreed cadence.
   - Use micro-slices (rs-*-a/b) to validate behavioral drift before wider exposure.

5) Post-rollout stabilization (24–72h)
   - Watch drift metrics (quality, cost per token, latencies) on 24h and 72h cadence.
   - Postmortem ingredients: timeline, steward notes, signal snapshots, user impact logs.

Steward role quick tasks (what to do, in order):
- 00:00 Preflight checklist (synth probes, dashboards)
- 00:05 Activate tiny slice, announce (channel + stakeholders)
- 00:10 Confirm no immediate errors, tag runbook snapshot
- 00:30 Re-evaluate; if green, approve next increment per matrix
- On signal breach: hit the circuit breaker, notify SRE, trigger fallback to previous model route
- After stabilization: update the rollout log in Confluence and close the experiment ticket

Steward communications snippets (copy-paste friendly):
- Start: "Rolling out model vX -> route Y to slice rs-20241115-01 at 0.5%. Steward: Aisha P. Watch window: 30m. Oncall: SRE-team. Escalation: see runbook."
- Pause/hold: "Holding ramp: p50 latency +50% over baseline in last 15m (rs-...). Investigating. No user-impacting rollback yet."
- Revert: "Reverting route Y -> vPrevious due to sustained error growth. All traffic redirected. Postmortem TBD."

Key signals and thresholds (starter set):
- Infrastructure / correctness:
  - 5xx rate > 0.5% absolute or 200% relative from baseline in 15m -> HOLD
  - p95 latency > SLO * 2 for 15m -> HOLD
- Quality / behavior:
  - Human-flag rate > baseline + 3x (or absolute 0.2%) in 1h -> REVIEW
  - Semantic divergence (evaluation metrics on sample set) drop > 6% -> REVIEW
- Cost / economic:
  - Avg token cost > 1.3x baseline for 1h -> HOLD and investigate quantization profile or a cheaper variant fallback

Common failure modes & immediate mitigations:
- Spike concentrated on one endpoint/route -> isolate slice to that endpoint and rollback only that route.
- Latency climbs due to KV cache thrash -> fallback to warm cache instance or increase cache shards.
- Model hallucination cluster -> disable generation fallback, route to deterministic reranker or rule-based response, notify Product.
- User complaint escalation -> assign to Solutions engineer for triage and set up short customer comms plan.

Experiment matrix (quick reference):
- Slice size / ramp schedule example: 0.5% -> 2% (1h) -> 10% (4h) -> 50% (12h) -> 100% (soft)
- Signal guard mapping: p95 latency (infra), human-flag (quality), 5xx (correctness), cost per 1k tokens (economics)
- Decision outcomes: CONTINUE / HOLD / ROLLBACK / PARTIAL-FIX + RE-RUN

Rehearsal checklist (run this at least once per quarter for steward rota):
- Synthetic traffic fail-over test (simulate 1% sudden growth)
- Comms drill: send a fake alert and confirm stakeholders get it and know the script
- Partial rollback rehearsal: perform a canary-level rollback to warm path and validate metrics return

Telemetry & dashboards (minimum widgets):
- Live: global request rate / slice rate, p50/p95/p99 latencies per slice, 5xx/error types, steady-state token cost.
- Behavioral: human-flag rate over rolling windows (5m/1h/6h), model divergence on golden prompts (hourly), top-20 user-agent breakdown.
- Slice health: per-slice synthetic probe success rate, per-slice error hotspots by route.

Runbook automation hooks (TODO for infra team):
- Auto-hold when any guard crosses threshold for 3 consecutive windows
- Automated snapshot of key dashboards and request traces on hold
- Lightweight rollback API call that re-points route mapping to prior version and runs a smoke probe

Postmortem starter template for steward to drop into Confluence:
- Title / short summary
- Timeline (activation times, observed breaches)
- Signals: charts + numeric deltas vs baseline
- Root cause hypothesis + evidence
- Actions taken and recovery steps
- Follow-ups (infra changes, model tuning, docs)

Notes to self / open questions (working):
- Do we want a "soft revert" that throttles generation temperature before full rollback? Pros: less UX churn; Cons: more complex transient state.
- How to standardize "golden prompt" set for semantic divergence across teams? Keep it small and stable.
- Can we add a low-cost cheap-model shadow path to catch behavior regressions early? (tradeoff: extra cost)

Short-term TODOs (owner tags):
- [ENG] add rollback API and api-key-scoped action (Marco)
- [SRE] implement auto-hold rule and snapshot (Lena)
- [OBS] add human-flag widget and set baseline (Priya)
- [Product] finalize steward escalation roster (Jonah)

Closing thought:
Treat the steward role as choreography — not firefighting. The better the rehearsal and signals, the less dramatic the symphony. Keep comms short, thresholds crisp, and automation boring (predictable).

-- end of cheatpad --

Editor notes: working draft, needs validation against ENG runbook and SLO docs. Will update with concrete metric IDs and links once infra hooks are in place.
